solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

indicators.note: something rejected is turned back, so the word for the complaint is read backwards

parts.note: flu is an illness, a complaint in the medical sense

explanation.surface: An engineer sends back a grievance from the town of Bury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bury' looks like the Lancashire town but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To engulf something is to swallow it up and cover it completely, which is to bury it.

definitions.meaning: a dump is slang for a bowel movement, a childish euphemism

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is nursery slang for a poo and also names a deputy or right-hand person.

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the run is read backwards
a piece of the two words is a run of letters taken from inside them

explanation.surface: Someone writes a childish article about an insect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece' takes TESPU from wriTES PUerile; 'about' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To bug someone is to annoy them, and to upset them is much the same.

clue.text: Loud female lifted man (supporter of Jack?)

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud

indicators.note: in a down clue lifted means raised up, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: a gal is a girl or woman
to man a place is to staff it

explanation.surface: A noisy woman picks up a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' turns GAL to LAG. The Union Jack is the British flag, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagpole holds up a flag such as the Union Jack, so it is a supporter of one.

clue.text: Shortly afterwards meets minister in seat of government

indicators.note: shortly says the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: then means afterwards, next
William Hague was a British government minister, Foreign Secretary

explanation.surface: Soon after, someone meets a minister in the place where the government sits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shortly' trims THEN to THE. William Hague is a former UK Foreign Secretary and Conservative leader.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch government and parliament sit in this city, although Amsterdam is the capital.

clue.text: God! One Direction actually there personally — which is irritating

parts.note: Thor is the Norse god of thunder
N, north, is one compass direction
in the flesh means present in person

explanation.surface: A fan gasps at seeing the boy band One Direction live, which annoys someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One Direction' looks like the pop band but is just one compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: A persistent source of annoyance or trouble is called this, after a phrase in St Paul's letters.

indicators.note: recycled means made over again, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: to tope is to drink heavily, so topes means drinks

explanation.surface: Reused beverages are served in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recycled' rearranges TOPES.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, to estop is to bar or preclude someone from asserting something.

parts.note: ado means fuss or trouble
a ration is an allotted share

explanation.surface: A question of whether romance always brings its portion of difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'share of trouble' is read as a share coming after trouble, so the share sits second.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is deep love and worship of someone.

indicators.note: a replay plays things again in a new way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: three of H, the abbreviation for hearts in cards
two of U, the abbreviation for United in team names

explanation.surface: A fan cheers a football result in which Hearts beat United three-two in a replayed cup tie.
explanation.walkthrough: Hearts (Heart of Midlothian) is a Scottish football club; the scores give three Hs and two Us.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal grunt of assent is an equivalent of saying yes casually.

indicators.note: not completely says the word is incomplete, missing its last letter

parts.note: amiss means wrong, out of order

explanation.surface: An author is only partly mistaken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not completely' drops the final S of AMISS. Kingsley and Martin Amis are both novelists.
explanation.definitionFit: Kingsley Amis and his son Martin are famous British novelists, so the surname names a writer.

clue.text: It's a feature of short piece from Alexander Pope work

indicators.note: work as a verb means knead or reshape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the poet's name with only a piece of his first name kept, his initial, gives the initial plus the surname

explanation.surface: A literary note on a brief extract from one of Alexander Pope's poems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' is the anagram signal, not the poem. The definition is witty: the punctuation mark is literally a feature of the word 'It's'.
explanation.definitionFit: The written word It's contains a raised comma marking the missing letter, so that mark is a feature of it.

clue.text: Dump in stream? Surprised it's acceptable

parts.note: a jet is a stream of liquid or gas

indicators.note: surprised suggests being thrown, so the letters of the short word are jumbled

parts.note: on means acceptable, as in 'that's not on'

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether it is all right to dump rubbish in a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surprised' rearranges IT'S to TIS.
explanation.definitionFit: To jettison cargo is to throw it overboard, so it means to dump or discard.

indicators.note: after places the word for hurting behind the exercise abbreviation

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise
achy means sore, hurting

explanation.surface: Feeling sore after a workout, but great all the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Peachy is informal for fine or splendid, as in 'everything is peachy'.

clue.text: Be ruthless in love, getting criticism at first

indicators.note: first puts the criticism and the little word ahead of the word for love

parts.note: stick means harsh criticism, as in 'took some stick'
love is nothing, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: Advice on romance: be hard-hearted, after first taking some flak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love' means zero, from tennis scoring, not affection.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who will stop at nothing to get what they want is ruthless; the idiom names that attitude.

parts.note: a throat is a maw; cut its last letter and maw becomes the clue's two letters

explanation.surface: Someone asks if Mum is a thug.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer, read as wordplay, cuts MAW (throat) short to give the clue's MA.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut-throat is a murderer or ruthless thug, a violent criminal.

clue.text: Reported one regularly popping up in town

indicators.note: reported means as said aloud, so the sound is what counts

parts.note: a kitchen toaster pops up the bread every time it is used

explanation.surface: A news report about someone who keeps appearing in a town.
explanation.walkthrough: TOWCESTER is a Northamptonshire town pronounced like 'toaster'.
explanation.definitionFit: Towcester is a market town in Northamptonshire, England.

clue.text: Doctor pinching seats at front, look! Be a man!

indicators.note: pinching means holding tight between the fingers, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor
a row is a line of seats in a theatre

indicators.note: the front of the word is its first letter

parts.note: an air is a look or manner

explanation.surface: A doctor takes the front seats and tells someone to toughen up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pinching' puts ROW and A (from 'at') between G and P.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang phrase is a crude command to show courage, much like telling someone to man up.

clue.text: After crash, owe two thousand — if it's gone, it's gone

indicators.note: a crash smashes things up, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: it is sex appeal, abbreviated SA

explanation.surface: After a financial crash you owe two thousand, and money that is lost is lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' is sex appeal, a crossword convention; 'gone' takes those letters out of the pool before 'crash' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Something out of the window has been abandoned or lost, as a hope or plan that has gone.

parts.note: Esc is the escape key on a keyboard
to hew is to cut with blows

explanation.surface: Steer clear of getting a key cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' is a keyboard key, not a musical one or one for a lock.
explanation.definitionFit: To eschew something is to deliberately abstain from it or shun it.

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the golfer's name

parts.note: Seve Ballesteros was a famous Spanish golfer
R is recipe, Latin for take, on prescriptions

explanation.surface: Sounds like advice to watch a golfer's first drive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening shot' is from tennis, not golf.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis and similar games each point begins with this stroke, the opening shot.

clue.text: Is touching up wife on top showing more understanding?

indicators.note: on top places the wife letter at the head of the down entry
in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: re means about, touching on

explanation.surface: Someone asks if fondling one's wife shows greater sensitivity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns RE to ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Being wiser means having more wisdom, so more understanding.

indicators.note: kicking knocks the letters about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boss's backside is crying out for a kick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bum' looks like a noun but is the verb, to cadge.
explanation.definitionFit: To bum a cigarette is to cadge it; living off others without paying is the same scrounging.

definitions.meaning: legal, permitted under the rules, in slang

explanation.definitionFit: As one word it is slang for lawful; split it is British slang for running away.

indicators.note: awkward suggests clumsy, out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The German capital is just too clumsy for celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a row of three bright stars in the constellation of the hunter.

definitions.meaning: a lecherous old man is called an old ...

explanation.surface: An instruction to assault a dirty old man.
explanation.definitionFit: Split into two words it means set about someone; as one, the animal is a byword for lust.

clue.text: Historian's opening chapter about old ruler

indicators.note: the opening of the word is just its first letter
about suggests moving around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A historian's book begins with a chapter on an ancient monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges CHAPTER to EPTARCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A heptarch was one of the rulers of the seven Anglo-Saxon kingdoms of early England.

parts.note: re means about, concerning
a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: Someone is about to give an incorrect reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as 'going to', but 'About' is RE and 'to' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A retort is a sharp reply, a kind of answer.
